items.headline: Tidal bans wholly AI-generated music from 9 December
items.summary: the policy was announced on 24 November, and Tidal says 43% of tracks delivered over the last 90 days were detected as wholly AI-generated.
items.matters: about 27 million tracks (6.3% of the catalogue) already carry its AI tag, 96% of them with no streams in three months and 94% from Suno. Deezer has not gone as far, and Bandcamp banned such music in January.
items.body:
The Block -owned streaming service says it will reject and remove “any wholly AI-generated track that’s submitted to Tidal,” starting on December 9.

Tracks that were “assisted by AI tools, but not the sole outputs, will be allowed on the platform,” according to the company.

Tidal says that 43% of all tracks distributed to it over the past 90 days were detected as wholly AI-generated.

The company has also named Ircam Amplify, the commercial subsidiary of French audio and music research institute IRCAM, as the technology partner behind its AI detection.

The policy update was announced on X on Tuesday (November 24) by Tidal and by Robert Andersen, Tidal Lead at Block.

“This year we introduced Tidal’s AI Policy to protect artists and keep listeners informed,” Tidal said in its post. “Since then, we’ve been identifying, labeling, and demonetizing tracks we determined are 100% AI generated outputs of tools like Suno, Lyria, and more.

On November 6, Tidal says it saw “the greatest influx of AI music yet,” with over 60% of the deliveries it received that day being wholly AI-generated.

The company added that, to date, it has automatically taken down more than 65,000 AI tracks over suspected impersonation of artist names.

“Tidal will always fight for artists to get paid more. Everything in this update comes back to that. If you make music, you should be able to put it on Tidal knowing it won’t be buried under tracks no one asked for, or copied by someone pretending to be you,” the company said.

Tidal ‘s ban goes further than the AI policy it introduced in June, which tagged wholly AI-generated music in its app and blocked it from earning royalties.

At the time, Tidal said it “will accept AI-generated music,” provided it met the standards in the policy and in its agreements with rightsholders and distributors.

Ircam Amplify describes itself as “the independent trust infrastructure for music in the age of AI,” and says it analyzes audio to assess the use of AI in tracks for streaming platforms, distributors, and collective management organizations.

Its AI Music Detector can analyze more than 250,000 tracks per hour, according to the product’s listing on IRCAM’s website.

Ircam Amplify launched its AI-Generated Detector in May 2024, when it said the tool could scan up to 5,000 tracks in under a minute with an accuracy rate of 98.5%.

items.headline: U2 debut "Torn", a Dolly Parton collaboration, at the first Thanksgiving Eve NFL game
items.summary: the Packers v Rams game on Netflix featured a halftime set with the Womack Sisters, and the song is described as Parton's final vocal recording.
items.matters: it follows the announcement of a 2027 North American stadium tour, with a BBC special from Tate Modern on Saturday and their Rock & Roll Hall of Fame performance on 8 December.
items.body:
Some might say, there's nothing like turkey and football. Some of those people might say there's nothing like U2 before turkey and football. And those people probably watched the first Thanksgiving Eve NFL game that happened last night. The game, which aired on Netflix, was between the Green Bay Packers and Los Angeles Rams. U2 performed the halftime show with Best New Artist Grammy nominees the Womack Sisters.

As U2 walked onto the field, a choir eerily recited the lyrics of "I Still Haven't Found What I'm Looking For." The band then began playing "Sunday Bloody Sunday." Later in the song, a drumline came on the field, followed by the Womack Sisters, who sang some of the Supremes' "Stop! In The Name Of Love." It was a cool mix.

As Bono sang the line "The trenches dug within our hearts/ And mothers, children, brothers, sisters torn apart," repeating it twice, U2 transitioned into the live debut of " Torn," the new Dolly Parton collaboration that marks her last vocal recording. As Parton's voice played over speakers, images of her smiling were projected on giant white sheets that hung over the stage.

U2 then played "Where The Streets Have No Name" and finished with "Pride (In The Name Of Love)," once again joined by the Womack Sisters. The Womack Sisters are the daughters of Cecil and Linda Womack, whose own musical project, Womack & Womack, once opened for U2. Linda Womack is also the daughter of soul legend Sam Cooke.

U2 announced their 2027 North American tour a few days ago. Earlier this month they filmed the BBC special U2: Live On The BBC At Tate Modern, premiering on Saturday, and a performance at the 2026 Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame induction ceremony, premiering Dec. 8.

As they reminded Rich Eisen this week, U2 played the Super Bowl almost 25 years ago. Bono called it their "kind of Ed Sullivan moment." He said, "we were just in this bewildering position of trying to put the grief and all the feelings that happened after 9/11 onto, the NFL gave us this opportunity. That was our moment."

items.headline: Matador takes worldwide rights to Belle and Sebastian's whole catalogue
items.summary: announced 25 November, with Bella Figura Music holding the two earliest albums and the rest licensed from the band.
items.matters: the first release is a 30th-anniversary edition of "If You're Feeling Sinister" (digital 20 January 2027, white-vinyl LP 26 February). Terms are undisclosed, and Bella Figura has spent about $160m on music rights so far.
items.body:
The Beggars Group label announced the deal on Wednesday (November 25), saying it has secured “worldwide rights” to the Glasgow band’s recordings.

Every title covered by the deal is held under license, with the rights split between Bella Figura Music and the band itself.

If You’re Feeling Sinister (1996) and The Boy With The Arab Strap (1998) are licensed from Bella Figura, along with the four EPs collected on Push Barman To Open Old Wounds, Volume 1 (2005).

Those titles were originally released by Jeepster and will carry both the Bella Figura and Matador names, according to the press release.

Albums originally released under Rough Trade in specific territories are licensed directly from the band.

The four records are Dear Catastrophe Waitress (2003), The Life Pursuit (2006), Write About Love (2010), and The Third Eye Centre (2013), plus their associated EPs and singles.

They will be branded as Matador/Rough Trade worldwide, carrying both labels’ logos in all territories.

The remaining seven albums, and their associated releases and EPs, are also licensed directly from Belle and Sebastian and will be released under the Matador name.

The five in between are Fold Your Hands Child, You Walk Like a Peasant (2000), Storytelling (2002), Girls in Peacetime Want to Dance (2015), Days of the Bagnold Summer (2019), and A Bit of Previous (2022).

In 1999, the label reissued the band’s 1996 debut, Tigermilk, which Matador says made the album widely available in North America for the first time.

Apart from 2003 ‘s Dear Catastrophe Waitress, which came out in the US through Rough Trade America, Matador has released all of the band’s subsequent records in North America.

Since 2015 ‘s Girls in Peacetime Want to Dance, it has also released the band’s output globally.

The first release under the new deal is a 30th anniversary edition of If You’re Feeling Sinister, which Matador announced on November 18.

It is accompanied by a bonus album, Lisa Helps The Blind, which features unreleased songs, early demos, and field recordings from the mid-1990s.

“The title came from a headline in the Glasgow Evening Times about a girl who was working with blind people,” writes frontman Stuart Murdoch in a liner notes essay on the bonus album.

The edition will be released digitally on January 20, 2027, with a white-vinyl LP of the original album alone following in stores on February 26.

items.headline: ElevenLabs is reportedly in early talks to raise at a $33bn valuation
items.summary: Bloomberg reported on 25 November that annual recurring revenue has reached about $700m.
items.matters: $33bn is about six times Suno's $5.4bn June valuation. ElevenLabs' music platform has licences with Merlin, Kobalt and Believe, plus a multi-year Universal deal from September.
items.body:
ElevenLabs is in early talks to raise new funding at a valuation of USD $33 billion.

That’s according to Bloomberg, which reported on Wednesday (November 25), citing people familiar with the matter.

The London – and New York -headquartered company plans to start the round in the first quarter of 2027, according to the report.

A $33 billion valuation would be 50% higher than the $22 billion ElevenLabs reached via a $300 million employee tender offer in September.

It would also be 10 times the $3.3 billion valuation attached to the company’s $180 million Series C round in January 2025.

The figure would be more than six times the $5.4 billion post-money valuation Suno reached in June via its own Series D.

The company said in May that it had crossed $500 million in ARR, up from $350 million at the end of 2025.

Co-founder and CEO Mati Staniszewski told TechCrunch in September that ARR had reached $600 million.

Its Series C, its first employee tender in September 2025, its Series D, and its third employee tender this September valued the company at $3.3 billion, $6.6 billion, $11 billion, and $22 billion, respectively.

Each of those figures – and the reported $33 billion target – is a multiple of the $1.1 billion valuation attached to its Series B in January 2024.

The $11 billion mark came via a $500 million Series D round announced in February, which was led by Sequoia Capital.

BDT & MSD, EQT, GIC, Goldman Sachs, Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan, and Sapphire Ventures invested in ElevenLabs for the first time as part of that transaction.

Proceeds from a tender go to the employees selling their existing shares, not to ElevenLabs itself.

ElevenLabs said at the time that enterprise customers accounted for 55% of its revenue, as businesses adopted its ElevenAgents conversational agent platform.

“AI should interact with people the way we interact with each other,” said Staniszewski, announcing the tender on September 30. “Getting this right will help ensure AI diffuses widely across the economy, and everyone is able to shape and benefit from it, regardless of technical skill.

On the music side, ElevenLabs launched its AI song generator, now called ElevenMusic, in August 2025.

Licensing deals with Merlin and publisher Kobalt were in place at launch, and the company has since added a deal with Believe.

Under that deal, ElevenLabs will launch an AI-powered music platform for fans, separate from ElevenMusic and its Music API.

items.headline: Worth watching this week: "The Tupac Tapes with Angie Martinez", out on Netflix today
items.summary: the four-part series is built around Martinez's long-withheld 1996 interview with Tupac, with commentary from Charlamagne Tha God, Joe Budden and others.
items.matters: I found no critical reviews yet, and early reaction is split between praise for Martinez's integrity and accusations of opportunism. Martinez says she held the tape back to avoid hurting people and escalating rivalries.
items.body:
Netflix has confirmed the global premiere date and trailer for 'The Tupac Tapes,' a four-part event featuring unreleased 1996 interview footage.

Netflix is expanding its audio-visual slate this fall with a major hip-hop event. The streamer has officially released the trailer for The Tupac Tapes with Angie Martinez, a four-part Netflix video podcast event set to premiere globally on November 27.

For nearly three decades, Radio Hall of Famer and New York Times bestselling author Angie Martinez has held onto one of the most sought-after pieces of hip-hop history: previously unreleased portions of her 1996 sit-down with Tupac Shakur, recorded in Los Angeles just months before his tragic murder. Now, for the first time ever, those tapes are being shared in full.

The newly released one-minute teaser sets a tense, reflective tone, blending archival footage from 1996 with modern roundtable discussions.

Speaking with Netflix about how the historic sit-down originally came together, Martinez recalled that Tupac initially reached out to ask her to appear in his music video for “I Ain’t Mad at Cha.” Though she declined due to the brewing coastal tensions, their phone conversation led to an invitation to his Los Angeles home—where he had New York pizza waiting for her—so he could clarify that his issues weren’t with the entirety of New York.

Explaining why she held back the full recordings for nearly 30 years, Martinez told Netflix:

For a long time, I didn’t feel comfortable releasing the tapes. There were things said in that conversation that could have hurt people, damaged relationships, and added fuel to an already dangerous situation… After Pac died, it became even more complicated. I felt a responsibility to protect something that was never meant to become his final statement.

But almost 30 years have passed. I also realized these tapes were bigger than me. They’re a piece of hip-hop history, and I don’t think they should just sit in my possession forever. The difference now is that I have the opportunity to share them with context.

I think people will be surprised by how much emotion is underneath everything he’s saying. We tend to remember Tupac as this fearless, confrontational figure, and he absolutely had that side. But when you listen closely, you also hear someone who’s hurt, who’s frustrated, who feels betrayed, and…

items.body:
A landmark partnership will see a dedicated CBeebies hub launch on Netflix UK this December before rolling out globally.

Netflix’s kids library is about to get a lot more British. The BBC and Netflix have announced a new partnership that will see a dedicated CBeebies hub launch on Netflix in the UK on December 2, with a global rollout also in the works and Netflix putting money into brand-new CBeebies shows.

Both companies are describing this as a limited trial. The BBC says it wants to test whether putting a sample of its preschool lineup on Netflix can extend CBeebies’ reach and visibility, and whether that viewing can be attributed back to the BBC.

Importantly, nothing is leaving the BBC’s own platforms. Every show in the trial stays on BBC iPlayer, which remains the home of the full CBeebies lineup alongside the linear channel and YouTube. The BBC stresses that the Netflix selection is only a small part of the wider CBeebies offering.

Netflix is no stranger to British preschool favorites, of course, with the likes of Shaun the Sheep and Hey Duggee already streaming. What’s different here is the branding: rather than individual licensed titles scattered across the kids catalog, CBeebies gets its own space.

The deal isn’t limited to the UK. BBC Studios has brokered a separate distribution deal that will bring the CBeebies brand experience to Netflix members outside the UK, with additional titles in the mix. No dates or title lists have been confirmed for international regions just yet.

There are some exceptions. The global deal does not include China, and the BBC notes that BBC Studios already has exclusive partnerships in place in New Zealand and South Africa.

Perhaps the most significant detail for the UK kids TV industry is that Netflix has committed to funding a small number of new CBeebies commissions as part of the partnership.

Netflix has spent the past year working hard to win over parents, and CBeebies is about as trusted as preschool brands get, especially in the UK and hopefully soon, globally. items.headline: AI Act gains two new bans from 2 December
items.summary: the Digital Omnibus on AI (Regulation (EU) 2026/1744) bans systems that generate non-consensual intimate imagery of identifiable people and AI-generated child sexual abuse material.
items.matters: providers are caught if that output is the intended purpose or a foreseeable, reproducible result without adequate safeguards, so image and video generators need filtering and refusal training (terms of use alone are not enough), and the Commission's guidelines do not yet cover these bans.
items.body:
Since 2 February 2025, eight categories of AI practices have been banned in the EU because they pose unacceptable risks to fundamental rights and Union values. These ‘prohibited practices’ are set out in Article 5 of the AI Act. In 2026, the Digital Omnibus added two further prohibitions, which apply from 2 December 2026. Breaching these prohibitions can attract the highest fines available under the AI Act: up to €35 million or 7% of an undertaking’s total worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher.

The European Commission’s Guidelines on prohibited AI practices explain how the Commission interprets the original eight prohibitions, set out the conditions that must be met for each to apply, and give examples of practices the Commission considers to fall inside or outside their scope. The Guidelines are not legally binding, and authoritative interpretation of the AI Act rests with the Court of Justice of the EU. Even so, they are the clearest indication of how the Commission expects Article 5 to work in practice.

This post summarises what the Guidelines say about the eight original prohibitions, and separately explains the two prohibitions added in 2026.

Before turning to the individual bans, the Guidelines clarify three important points about their scope.

First, Article 5 can apply to both providers of AI systems and their deployers. Their responsibilities are different: providers are responsible for the systems they place on the market or put into service, while deployers are responsible for how they use them.

Finally, an AI system that falls outside an Article 5 prohibition is not necessarily unregulated. It may still be classified as high-risk, and other EU rules, including data protection and consumer law, may continue to apply.

Our goal is to build the most useful, authoritative, and comprehensive guide to the AI Act anywhere on the internet. We’ll never put this behind a paywall or use it to sell you a service. We do this because we think good AI governance matters, and that means making authoritative guidance genuinely accessible.

This website is built and maintained by the Future of Life Institute — the world’s oldest and largest nonprofit working for the responsible development of AI.

Each prohibition has its own conditions and, in some cases, exceptions. A practice falls within a particular prohibition only where its relevant conditions are met. Below are the clarifications which may be most relevant in practice.

items.headline: Italian regulator fines Meta €805 million over Facebook's gallery-suggestion feature (decision 13 November)
items.summary: the DPA found Meta never got specific, informed consent to read Android photo galleries, because one system permission covered several functions and the feature was on by default.
items.matters: Meta must add a separate consent request within 60 days and keep the feature off by default, and the ePrivacy-based decision sidesteps the GDPR one-stop-shop, so any app bundling device-permission prompts is exposed to national regulators.
items.body:
The Italian Data Protection Authority (DPA) launched an investigation following a complaint submitted in July 2025 by the Bolzano Consumer Protection Centre concerning Facebook's access to users' smartphone photo galleries. The investigation focused on the feature “Get suggestions from your gallery while browsing Facebook”, which displays photos and videos stored on Android devices as suggestions for sharing on the social network. The Authority carried out a technical analysis of the feature and examined whether Meta had obtained valid consent and adequately informed users before accessing information stored on their devices.

The investigation found that Facebook requested a single system permission to access photos and videos for several different functions. The request was preceded by a generic notice referring to enabling other features, without clearly explaining that access would also enable gallery suggestions. The feature was enabled by default, although it could operate only after system permission had been granted. Once authorised, the app could access the device's multimedia archive on an ongoing basis. The DPA found that Meta had not obtained specific, informed consent for this feature, in breach of Article 122 of the Italian Data Protection Code. The Authority rejected Meta's jurisdictional objection, noting that the ePrivacy framework does not provide for the GDPR's One-Stop-Shop mechanism.

The Italian DPA imposed an administrative fine of EUR 805 million on Meta Platforms Ireland Limited. It ordered Meta, within 60 days of notification, to introduce a separate, specific consent request, provide clear information and keep the feature disabled by default, including for existing users. If Meta fails to comply, the feature must not operate without valid consent. Meta must report initial measures within 30 days and provide implementation details within 90 days. The Authority considered the approximately 20 million Android users potentially affected in Italy, the duration of the infringement, a previous sanction and insufficient cooperation. The fine represents approximately 0.47% of the group's worldwide turnover.

items.headline: Commission proposes the Quantum Act and a Sovereign Tech Equity Fund
items.summary: the proposal has three pillars (research excellence, adoption, security of systems and supply chains) and aims to prepare Europe's digital systems for post-quantum cryptography.
items.matters: it is only a proposal and the page gives no budget, but post-quantum cryptography migration is the part that could eventually touch anyone shipping software with long-lived encrypted data.
items.body:
The European Commission today proposed the Quantum Act, a new framework to help turn Europe's quantum research into products and services, strengthen supply chains and prepare Europe's digital systems for post-quantum cryptography.

The Quantum Act has three main pillars: research excellence, bringing quantum technology into use, and keeping systems and supplies secure. These will be delivered through the Quantum Europe Framework Initiative, which will bring together EU and national programmes around shared priorities for research and industry.

"Quantum technologies will shape the future of industry, security and innovation, and they will have a profound impact on our societies. Europe needs to accelerate now. With the Quantum Act, we are putting in place the key elements to turn our world-class quantum research into industrial capacity, strengthen critical supply chains and prepare for the cyber risks linked to quantum computing. Europe has already built strong foundations in quantum; now we must turn them into industrial scale, resilient supply chains and secure deployment."

items.headline: Irish regulator fines Tinder's owner MTCH €11 million over "Download My Data"
items.summary: the tool omitted some personal data or gave only summaries while being presented as a full copy of users' data.
items.matters: MTCH has three months to comply, so a data-export feature that is not complete counts as a breach of the access right.
items.body:
The Data Protection Commission (DPC) has today announced its final decision following an Inquiry into MTCH Technology Services Limited (“MTCH”), concerning its Tinder service. This own-volition Inquiry was launched by the DPC in January 2020, in its role as the Lead Supervisory Authority for MTCH.

This decision concerns MTCH’s failure to provide Tinder users with a complete copy of their personal data on request, pursuant to Article 15(3) GDPR. In particular, the DPC assessed the operation of a self-service tool on Tinder (known as the Download My Data tool), which enabled users to download their data.

Although this tool was presented to users as a way to obtain a copy of their Tinder data, the DPC found that it failed to provide users with all of their personal data. Certain categories of information were omitted without notice to the user, or provided in summary form only. The DPC also found that the personal data provided through the tool did not meet the requirements of the right of access under the GDPR.

The DPC’s decision found that MTCH infringed Article 15(3) by failing to provide a copy of personal data in circumstances where, MTCH made available an automated tool (known as the Download My Data tool), and described this automated tool as a means to 'request a copy' of personal data without otherwise making clear that the tool did not provide access to certain personal data.

The DPC has imposed administrative fines totalling EUR 11 million and has ordered MTCH to bring its processing into compliance within 3 months.

items.headline: Bearman stays at Haas for 2027
items.summary: the re-signing was confirmed as the paddock reached Qatar, making it his third full-time season with the team, and he says his "dream is to race for Ferrari".
items.matters: the contract length isn't given, and Bearman remains in Ferrari's junior ranks, so the Ferrari door is not closed.
items.body:
Ollie Bearman arrives into the Qatar Grand Prix weekend with his future finally confirmed, following the announcement that he will continue to drive for Haas in 2027.

Ollie Bearman has shared his reaction following the long-awaited confirmation that he will continue to drive for Haas in 2027, with the Briton reflecting on his immediate goal going forward while also admitting that, in the long-term, his “dream is to race for Ferrari”.

Despite the expectation being that he would remain with Haas next season, the news had still yet to be officially announced last time out at the Las Vegas Grand Prix, leading Bearman to concede that it was “disappointing” to be at that stage of the campaign without having the situation resolved.

However, it was finally announced just as the F1 paddock arrived in Qatar for the penultimate event of the year that Bearman had re-signed with the American outfit, marking his third full-time season racing for the team.

“We got there in the end,” the 21-year-old explained during media day at the Lusail International Circuit.

Pushed on the goal that he has set for himself and Haas in 2027, Bearman responded: “Well, nothing yet. It depends how fast the car is, right? We're trying to make it as fast as possible, and then we see.

Bearman remains a part of Ferrari ’s junior programme and previously made his F1 debut for the Scuderia when he stood in for an unwell Carlos Sainz at the 2024 Saudi Arabian Grand Prix, a race that saw the British driver also score his maiden points with a P7 finish.

Asked if there was confidence that he would get his chance with Ferrari in the future, Bearman said: “I hope so. I would say that I'm here thanks to Ferrari.

“I don't know, if I didn't get that chance in Jeddah [in 2024], if I would be sitting here right now, so I'm incredibly grateful to Ferrari for the opportunities they gave me, for putting me in the car as an 18-year-old – I think that was a pretty big risk and it paid off.

For now Bearman stated that his immediate outlook is the “continuation with Haas”, while he also hopes that becoming the most experience driver in the squad – with rookie Rafael Camara joining as his team mate – can prove his worth to the top teams.

“I think it's definitely interesting. It's something to work towards, right?” Bearman said of the leadership role. “If you want to be successful or go anywhere in Formula 1, I think you need to prove that you're capable of leading a team.

items.headline: Russell shrugs off Verstappen's Las Vegas jibes
items.summary: Russell called the post-race comments "quite amusing" and said he wants to move on. He stands by his "somebody has got to stand up to that guy" remark but says he respects Verstappen's driving "immensely".
items.matters: Verstappen won in Las Vegas after Russell locked up chasing teammate Antonelli, hit the barriers and fell to ninth. The feud follows them into Qatar, where practice is Friday and the race is Sunday at 17:00.
items.body:
After tensions between himself and Max Verstappen resurfaced following the Las Vegas Grand Prix, George Russell has given his take on how the situation stands.

George Russell has given his reaction to Max Verstappen’s comments about him following the Las Vegas Grand Prix, with the Briton now looking to switch his focus to the race weekend ahead in Qatar after the “quite amusing” remarks.

The rivalry between the two drivers – which stretches back more than three years – was reignited in Nevada following an incident during third practice, which led to Russell stating that “somebody has got to stand up to that guy” off the back of Verstappen receiving a warning from the stewards.

Race day saw the pair line up alongside each other on the front row of the grid before engaging in a long fight for the lead, with Verstappen continuously retaking P1 whenever he had been briefly overtaken by the Mercedes driver.

Kimi Antonelli later moved ahead of Russell into second place, with the British racer then trying to overtake his team mate in the closing stages – a move that backfired when he locked up and hit the barriers, dropping him down to ninth place while Verstappen took victory up ahead.

Following the race, Verstappen labelled Russell as “so far below my level” and said he had found it “fantastic” to see the Silver Arrows car go off track behind him in his mirrors.

When asked on media day ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix about the situation, Russell suggested that he could see the funny side as he answered: “I don't really have much to say, to be honest.

Pushed on whether he wanted to say anything in response to Verstappen’s remarks, the 28-year-old said: “No, not really, to be honest. Not really. At the end of the day, I guess I stand by what I said after practice, but he was the one who went out and won the race.

Russell went on to underline that his focus is on succeeding behind the wheel, adding that “it’s not a war of words off track” and that he respects Verstappen “immensely for his driving talent and everything he's achieved on track, and that's that really”.

Verstappen was also quizzed on the situation when speaking to the media in Qatar and – when asked if he approaches his battles with Russell on the track differently to his relationship with him off it – the Red Bull driver responded: “During the race you just try to focus on getting the best result out of it, and everything else that has been said off track has been said.

“There's nothing else to add, and also from my side of course, just happy to win in Vegas.

items.body:
After contact limited them to the lower end of the points in Las Vegas, Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton have insisted they’re working towards a solution to avoid further intra-team incidents.

Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton have opened up on the mood within Ferrari after they clashed during the Las Vegas Grand Prix, with the former admitting that “we’re all disappointed” despite ongoing efforts to improve their on-track relationship.

Following incidents in Italy and Mexico, the pair made contact when Leclerc attempted a pass on his team mate in Las Vegas, resulting in a 10-second time penalty that dropped the Monegasque to P10 in the final classification.

An unrelated penalty for Hamilton contributed to his own P7 finish and rounded out a frustrating weekend for the Scuderia, especially as both had made significant progress after being eliminated in the second stage of Qualifying.

Although Team Principal Fred Vasseur previously confirmed that he had held talks to address how they race one another, he lamented their "lack of respect” in the “unacceptable” episode – a comment Leclerc readily agreed with.

“Fred had already talked on the radio, telling me he wanted to speak to me before [I went] to the media, so I obviously knew where Fred was standing,” Leclerc explained during media duties in Qatar. “As a driver, you’ve got to accept that.

“As a team, we cannot afford to clash between team mates. I think that is very clear for everyone. For the clash in particular in Las Vegas, I took responsibility. I think there’s tension around that we just need to dissipate and make sure that we look at more positive days in the future. That’s all I’m looking for.

He also admitted that he and Hamilton had already spoken ahead of Round 21 in Qatar, but was reluctant to disclose what “solutions” had been proposed within the team.

“We have a very good relationship outside of the car with Lewis,” he said. “I wouldn’t say the atmosphere is good because obviously we are all disappointed with the situation we find ourselves in.

“At the same time, we’re all grown up and responsible so we’ve got to find a solution. Surely there’s not a super happy feeling at the moment. We are the ones that need to find a solution in order to make that better.

“The only thing that I don’t like seeing is people questioning my integrity to the team, my love for the team. I’ve been in Ferrari since 2019. I think there is nothing clearer than the love I have for the team. I’ll do absolutely everything in order to bring Ferrari back to the top.

items.headline: Longreads and Vittles on how M.F.K. Fisher quietly helped make Japanese food fine dining in America
items.summary: Vaughn Tan's essay (24 November, about 4,000 words, roughly 17 minutes) draws on Fisher's uncatalogued papers. He argues she ran an unseen campaign from 1979 to 1982 that promoted Shizuo Tsuji's "Japanese Cooking: A Simple Art" through trusted critics and editors.
items.matters: it is a close look at how influence works through people who pass ideas along without credit, and at how the cuisine that caught on was a selective version.
items.body:
This essay is co-published with Vittles and appears in Vittles Issue No. 3: The Influencers.

Back in 2003, I was in the early stages of researching how the distinctive visual style of Japanese plating and dish design influenced plating outside Japan, and wanted to analyze photos of fine-dining dishes in industry periodicals like Art Culinaire. Back in the early 2000s, this was easiest to do in libraries. At the time, I lived in Cambridge, Massachusetts, so I wound up in the collection of historical cookbooks and culinary materials at the Schlesinger Library.

One afternoon, Barbara Haber, then the Schlesinger’s curator of books, stopped by my desk with something for me: Japanese Cooking: A Simple Art by Shizuo Tsuji, published in 1980 with an introduction by MFK Fisher. I knew of Fisher through her essays on eating and her translation of Brillat-Savarin’s The Physiology of Taste, but not for anything related to Japanese food. Barbara mentioned that many boxes of Fisher’s collected papers had recently arrived at the library. The papers were still uncatalogued, but was I interested in looking at them?

I didn’t know then that I was beginning a 20-year detour. As I went through these boxes over the next few months, my original research project faded away. I found myself more and more drawn to the Fisher archive boxes, and to the story that emerged as I read through years of her correspondence and other documents, including letters about her trip to Japan to research the introduction she wrote to Japanese Cooking; letters about the book she wrote to journalists, writers, and editors across the US; and draft manuscripts of Japanese Cooking, with her comments in red pen, which had crisscrossed the Pacific between California and Osaka. The story that emerged was of a secret campaign Fisher waged between 1979 and 1982, which was instrumental in the seemingly sudden transformation of Japanese food into fine dining in America.

The Fisher I uncovered in those boxes was someone else, and her role in making Japanese food into fine dining in America remains almost entirely unknown.

Fisher’s campaign worked well because it was largely invisible. The publishers of Japanese Cooking didn’t know that any of this was happening. Ruth Reichl, who wrote the foreword to the 25th anniversary edition in 2005, had no idea Fisher had done any more than write the introduction when I spoke to her earlier this year.
